comment: RS (Edexcel IGCSE 4RS1, Christianity) multiple choice — Paper 1 Section 2, spec points 2.3 to 2.8 (sanctity of life, abortion and euthanasia; human relationships; marriage and partnership; divorce and remarriage; family; childlessness and celibacy). Built from the specification and the Section 2 revision booklet because these topics have not been taught in class yet. Ids continue from mcq-bank-1.json, which holds M1-M30 for this module. NOTE: this file still needs adding to the rs mcqBanks list in tools/subjects.js.

02-life-and-death.q: The sanctity of life is the belief that…
options: every life should be as happy as possible
life is a sacred gift from God, so it is not ours to end
life is valuable because people are useful to society
02-life-and-death.explain: Two halves: life is intrinsically valuable because it is God's gift, and it is not for humans to decide when it ends. The 'happiness' option is the quality-of-life view instead.

02-life-and-death.q: Which verse gives Christians the doctrine of imago Dei?
02-life-and-death.explain: Genesis 1:27 — 'So God created mankind in his own image'. Genesis 2:24 is 'one flesh' (marriage), Exodus 20:13 is 'you shall not murder', Psalm 139:13 is being knitted together in the womb.

02-life-and-death.q: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you' comes from…
02-life-and-death.explain: Jeremiah 1:5 — the key anti-abortion text, used to argue that God knows and plans for a person before birth.

02-life-and-death.q: Abortion in the UK is governed by…
02-life-and-death.explain: The Abortion Act 1967. Two doctors must agree 'in good faith' that one of the legal grounds is met; the Suicide Act 1961 is the euthanasia and assisted-suicide law.

02-life-and-death.q: In most cases, the upper time limit for a legal abortion in the UK is…
02-life-and-death.explain: 24 weeks, set by amendment in 1990. There is no time limit where there is a risk to the woman's life, a risk of grave permanent injury to her health, or a substantial risk of serious disability.

02-life-and-death.q: Under UK law, assisting someone to end their own life is…
options: a criminal offence carrying up to 14 years in prison
legal if the person is terminally ill
02-life-and-death.explain: The Suicide Act 1961 decriminalised suicide and attempted suicide, but assisting a suicide remains an offence punishable by up to 14 years. Actively ending another person's life is murder or manslaughter, so euthanasia is illegal.

02-life-and-death.q: Ending a person's life without their consent because they cannot express a wish — for example someone in a persistent vegetative state — is called…
02-life-and-death.explain: Non-voluntary: the person cannot say. Voluntary is at their own request; involuntary is against their wishes; assisted suicide means the person ends their own life with help.

02-life-and-death.q: Agape means…
options: love of God for the saved only
02-life-and-death.explain: Agape is the selfless, self-giving love described in 1 Corinthians 13. Liberal Christians make it the one absolute, which is the basis of situation ethics and of the 'most loving option' argument.

02-life-and-death.q: 'Love is patient, love is kind' comes from…
02-life-and-death.explain: 1 Corinthians 13:4, in the chapter that ends 'the greatest of these is love' (13:13). Mark 12:31 is 'love your neighbour as yourself'.

02-life-and-death.q: Which text do conservative Christians most often cite against same-sex sexual relationships?
02-life-and-death.explain: Leviticus 18:22, with Romans 1:26-27 and the appeal to male and female in Mark 10:6-9. Genesis 1:27 and Galatians 3:28 are used on the affirming side.

02-life-and-death.q: The Roman Catholic Catechism describes homosexual acts as…
02-life-and-death.explain: 'Intrinsically disordered' (Catechism 2357). The same teaching insists that people with a homosexual inclination 'must be accepted with respect, compassion, and sensitivity' (2358) and are called to chastity (2359) — so the act, not the person, is condemned.

02-life-and-death.q: 'They become one flesh', used to argue that marriage creates a single new unit, is from…
02-life-and-death.explain: Genesis 2:24, which Jesus quotes in Mark 10:6-9. Genesis 1:28 is 'be fruitful and increase in number'; Ephesians 5:25 tells husbands to love their wives as Christ loved the church.

02-life-and-death.q: Which denomination has celebrated same-sex marriages on the same basis as any other since its 2009 decision?
02-life-and-death.explain: The Quakers (Britain Yearly Meeting). The Methodist Church in Britain followed in 2021; the Church of England keeps its doctrine of marriage but authorised prayers of blessing for same-sex couples in 2023.

02-life-and-death.q: An annulment is…
options: a declaration that no valid marriage ever existed
a divorce granted by a priest
a blessing after a civil wedding
02-life-and-death.explain: The Roman Catholic alternative to divorce: because a valid sacramental marriage cannot be dissolved, the Church may instead declare that no valid marriage existed — for example because of deceit, coercion or incapacity at the time of the vows.

02-life-and-death.q: In Matthew 19:9 Jesus allows divorce on the single ground of…
02-life-and-death.explain: Matthew 19:9 — 'except for sexual immorality'. Desertion by an unbeliever is Paul's exception (1 Corinthians 7:15); Mark 10:9 allows no exception at all. Those three strands explain why the churches differ.

02-life-and-death.q: Catholic teaching calls the family the 'domestic church' because…
options: families should hold services at home instead of attending church
the parish is run by families
it is where faith is first taught and handed on
only married couples may receive communion
02-life-and-death.explain: The family is where children are brought to baptism, taught to pray and raised 'in the training and instruction of the Lord' (Ephesians 6:4) — so it functions as a church in miniature, which is why churches invest in supporting it.

02-life-and-death.q: Roman Catholic teaching permits natural family planning but forbids the condom and the pill because…
options: the couple abstain rather than alter the act itself, so no marital act is deliberately closed to life
the Bible explicitly forbids artificial devices
natural methods are cheaper and so available to the poor
02-life-and-death.explain: The Natural Law objection is to interfering with the act, not to the intention. Natural family planning restricts sex to infertile days without altering the act, so Catholic teaching accepts it. Critics reply that the intention is identical either way.

02-life-and-death.q: Humanae Vitae (1968) teaches that…
options: contraception is a matter for the couple's own conscience
IVF may be used by married couples
celibacy is required of every Christian
every marital act must remain open to the transmission of life
02-life-and-death.explain: Paul VI's Humanae Vitae is the Catholic teaching against artificial contraception. The 'matter of conscience' option is the Anglican position, which goes back to the Lambeth Conference of 1930.

02-life-and-death.q: AID differs from AIH in that…
options: AID uses a donor's sperm while AIH uses the husband's
AID is carried out in a clinic and AIH at home
AID uses the husband's sperm while AIH uses a donor's
AID always involves a surrogate mother
02-life-and-death.explain: Artificial Insemination by Donor brings a third party's genetic material into the marriage — which Catholic teaching has called a kind of mechanical adultery. Artificial Insemination by Husband keeps both gametes within the marriage, which is why many Protestants accept it and reject AID.

02-life-and-death.q: Which document sets out the Roman Catholic rejection of IVF?
02-life-and-death.explain: Donum Vitae. Humanae Vitae is on contraception, Amoris Laetitia is on marriage and the pastoral care of the remarried, and Evangelium Vitae is the 'culture of death' encyclical on abortion and euthanasia.

02-life-and-death.q: Celibacy is…
options: abstaining from sex until you are married
the settled choice to abstain from sexual activity, usually also from marriage
the right ordering of sexual behaviour for whatever state of life you are in
a vow taken by all Christians at confirmation
02-life-and-death.explain: The other two tempting options describe chastity, not celibacy — for an unmarried Christian chastity means abstinence, and for a married one it means faithfulness. Mixing the two words up costs a definition mark.

02-life-and-death.q: Which Christian ministers are required to be celibate?
options: Roman Catholic priests of the Latin Church, together with monks and nuns
02-life-and-death.explain: Anglican and Methodist clergy may marry; the Orthodox churches ordain married men as parish priests but choose their bishops from among the celibate. Paul's argument for celibacy is that the unmarried person 'is concerned about the Lord's affairs' (1 Corinthians 7:32–33).

02-life-and-death.q: Matthew 19:12 — 'others have renounced marriage because of the kingdom of heaven' — is used to argue that…
options: divorce is permitted on the ground of adultery
a life without marriage or children is a genuine Christian calling
02-life-and-death.explain: It is the key text both for celibacy and for accepting voluntary childlessness: Jesus treats renouncing marriage as a real vocation, while adding 'the one who can accept this should accept it' — so it is a gift given to some, not a rule for all.

02-life-and-death.q: The difference between adoption and fostering is that…
options: fostering is permanent and adoption is temporary
adoption is arranged by churches and fostering by local councils
adoption transfers parental responsibility permanently, while fostering is temporary care
02-life-and-death.explain: In fostering, legal responsibility stays with the birth parents or the local authority and the child may return home. Christians support both, citing James 1:27 — looking after orphans is 'pure and faultless' religion — and Ephesians 1:5, where adoption is Paul's image for salvation itself.

02-life-and-death.q: Therapeutic cloning is…
options: cloning cells, not a person, to grow tissue for treating illness
producing a new human being genetically identical to the donor
screening IVF embryos for genetic disease
freezing spare embryos for later use
02-life-and-death.explain: Many Protestant churches accept therapeutic cloning because it heals, while rejecting reproductive cloning — which is in any case banned in humans in the UK by the Human Reproductive Cloning Act 2001. Catholic teaching rejects human cloning as immoral and unnecessary.

02-life-and-death.q: Which verse is most often used against a couple deliberately choosing to have no children?
02-life-and-death.explain: Genesis 1:28 — 'be fruitful and increase in number' — read as a command given in creation, backed by Psalm 127:3 calling children 'a heritage from the LORD'. Genesis 2:18, Matthew 19:12 and 1 Corinthians 7:9 are all used on the other side of the argument.

02-life-and-death.q: Passive euthanasia is…
options: a lethal injection given at the patient's own request
providing someone with the means to end their own life
death that follows from withdrawing or withholding life-sustaining treatment
ending a life against the person's expressed wishes
02-life-and-death.explain: The others are active euthanasia, assisted suicide and involuntary euthanasia. The distinction matters because Catholic teaching permits discontinuing burdensome or futile treatment while forbidding any act or omission intended to cause death.

02-life-and-death.q: Marriage is regarded as a sacrament by…
options: the Roman Catholic and Orthodox churches
the Church of England and the Methodist Church
02-life-and-death.explain: A sacrament is an outward sign of inward grace. Catholics and Orthodox treat marriage as one, which is why a valid consummated marriage cannot be dissolved and annulment is offered instead of divorce; most Protestants call marriage a covenant made before God but not a sacrament.
